title: constraints
description: INPUT CONTRACT for the asset-processing table's row-11 artifact ('IP user guide / digital+analog doc -> constraints.md: timing, electrical limits, untestable items -> exemption list'). Transcribed from a real IP user guide or analog/digital datasheet; dv_harness/design_intent.py validates it, renders docs/constraints.md, and -- the load-bearing part -- converts every `untestable_items` entry into a real exemption record conforming to exemptions.schema.json, so an untestable item becomes a tracked, expiring, owned exemption rather than a sentence in a document nobody re-reads. That conversion is why `owner` and `valid_until` are REQUIRED here: exemptions.schema.json requires them and has no 'no expiry' escape hatch, so an untestable item that cannot name an owner and a review date cannot silently become a permanent unchecked hole.

unit.description: e.g. 'ns', 'us'. Required in practice whenever any of min/typ/max is present -- a bare number with no unit is not a constraint.

untestable_items.description: Things the IP documentation states cannot be verified in this environment (analog behaviour with no digital observable, a feature needing real silicon, a mode the delivered model does not implement). Each becomes a real exemption record.

check_id.description: The concrete check/assertion/coverage bin this exempts, matching exemptions.schema.json's own check_id field. A blanket 'everything analog' is not acceptable -- an exemption must name what it turns off.

category.description: Why it is untestable. Recorded so a later reviewer can re-evaluate the whole class at once when, say, a better model arrives.

owner.description: The human accountable for re-reviewing this. Required because exemptions.schema.json requires it.

valid_until.description: ISO 8601 review date. Required because exemptions.schema.json requires it and offers no 'no expiry' value.
